headline: Test 2: Virginia, 1640–1705 · 45:10

items.title: 45:10 · Step one arrived in July 1640 in
items.detail: Step one arrived in July 1640 in the case of John Punch, adjudicated by the Virginia Governor's Council.

items.title: 45:17 · Three servants of the planter Hugh Gwyn
items.detail: Three servants of the planter Hugh Gwyn ran away together toward Maryland and were recaptured: a Dutchman named Victor, a Scotsman named James Gregory, and a Black man named John Punch.

items.title: 45:29 · The Virginia Council sentenced all three men
items.detail: The Virginia Council sentenced all three men to thirty lashes each and added four years of service to the indentures of the Dutchman and the Scotsman.

items.title: 45:40 · For the third runaway the Council ordered
items.detail: For the third runaway, the Council ordered that John Punch serve his master or his assigns for the time of his natural life.

items.title: 45:49 · That 1640 sentencing differential is the first
items.detail: That 1640 sentencing differential is the first recorded American judicial compilation of Equation 3.10, making permanent bondage a function of African phenotype specifically to split a three-man cross-racial runaway coalition.
